findings.desc: learning-store.ts:approveSignatureTag (line ~222) auto-creates a never-proposed tag directly as status=active, bypassing the propose step. CHK-003 adversarial:0 specifies 'rejected OR auto-creates as proposed then requires re-approve' — neither option is implemented. The verificationEvidence for CHK-003:adversarial:0 cites the smoke, but the smoke does not assert this adversarial path. Suggest: either add an assert.throws test for approve-on-unregistered in the smoke, or document the deliberate behavior deviation in the handler comment and checklist.
findings.resolvedReason: approveSignatureTag now rejects approving a never-proposed tag (throws 'has not been proposed'); idempotent on already-active. Smoke check 'CHK-003:adversarial:0 approve never-proposed rejected' + 'CHK-003:edge:1 idempotent approve' added. Commit fbfec03824.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:2 lacks valid verificationEvidence: intent requires resolveEvidenceStrength="" (empty string) -> rejected, but validateOptionalEnum() in finding.ts treats empty string as undefined and returns silently without throwing (line: `if (value === undefined || value === null || value === "") return undefined`). The smoke validation check only tests an invalid non-empty string ("super") and never exercises the empty-string path. No evidence record specifically binds this intent to a check that proves rejection of empty strings.
findings.resolvedReason: validateOptionalEnum now rejects an explicitly-provided empty/whitespace enum string (undefined still = omitted); applies to all enum fields. Smoke check 'CHK-002:adversarial:2 empty-string enum rejected' added. Commit fbfec03824.

findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:0,1,2,3 and CHK-003:edge:1 — five must-priority intents have no corresponding smoke check. (1) adversarial:0: approve on a tag that was never proposed — no check; (2) adversarial:1: action="DROP_TABLE" invalid enum — handler validates this but no smoke check asserts it; (3) adversarial:2: self-alias (tag=aliasOf) — no check; (4) adversarial:3: concurrent finding_add with different signatureTags — no check; (5) edge:1: signature_registry_set approve on already-active tag is idempotent — no check. All five evidence records point to npm run test:experience-layer-finding-enums and claim pass, but the smoke contains no named check for any of these behaviors. This is a command-binding mismatch: the evidence command does not literally execute the verification described in the intent.
